WSP Parsons Brinckerhoff and DNV GL (2015). Industrial Decarbonisation and Energy Efficiency Roadmaps to 2050: Oil Refining (main report and Appendices A-D). Prepared for the Department of Energy and Climate Change (DECC) and the Department for Business, Innovation and Skills (BIS), London, March 2015. No DOI or report number printed. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/industrial-decarbonisation-and-energy-efficiency-roadmaps-to-2050

Locators are printed page numbers: "Report p.N" = footer of the 88-page main report; "App. p.N" = footer of the 80-page Appendices. UK, 2012 base year. Main file (5 technologies): whole-site CCS options with capex per representative site (GBP 138 million on CHP and hydrogen plant stacks, GBP 125.5 million on FCC stacks, both for a nominal 2.3 Mt CO2/yr site, capture only), TRL, whole-refinery CO2 reduction (as emissions-reduction-potential, not a capture rate), CDU temperature 380 degC, fired heater 250-500 degC, CHP/turbine lifespan. Other option capex are per representative site but with no capacity or equipment boundary, so all 22 register options (Tables 10 and 11) are in _measures with the printed CO2 (or electricity) reduction of the whole site, TRL, adoption and applicability. Not loaded: Appendix D deployment charts (adoption percentages by year), social/business findings. Traps: the register gives GBP 8.5 billion for a replacement refinery but main report Sect. 3.3.5 says GBP 4-5 billion; cost price year not stated anywhere; "CO2 (C) or electricity (E) reduction" is a single column with the type in brackets; reduction percentages are shares of whole-site emissions (or electricity), not of the equipment they apply to.
